# Coordinated unrotation escapes the rotated-triangle radial trap

The exact radial trap in
candidate 92e51a4b18979d56
admits a strict FIRST-ORDER nonradial escape. Both endpoint triangles
move, and the middle fiber remains their exact Minkowski average at
every stage. The three original cylindrical cap planes are fixed.
Total mixed mass increases and every selected cap mass decreases.

Thus neither a free-fiber assumption nor preliminary strictification
is needed. The result concerns this particular selected minimal
three-cap cover, not a general cap-cover classification or OC.

## 1. An exact compatible family

Let K be the centered standard triangle, of area 1/2, and
\[
 J=\begin{pmatrix}-1&-2\\2&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 A_t=(I+tJ)K,\quad B_t=(I-tJ)K,\quad D_t=(A_t+B_t)/2.
\]
Use these at integer bases -1,0,1 and set
\[
 C_t=\operatorname{conv}\big(\{-1\}\times A_t
                       \ \cup\ \{1\}\times B_t\big).
\]
Then C_t is an actual full three-dimensional convex body, with
projection [-1,1] and EXACTLY the three integer fibers A_t,D_t,B_t.
The midpoint relation remains equality, not a relaxed inequality.

For 0<t<1/3, the endpoint vertices are
\[
 \begin{split}
 A_t:&\quad(-1/3+t,-1/3-t),\ (2/3,-1/3+t),\
                                      (-1/3-t,2/3),\\
 B_t:&\quad(-1/3-t,-1/3+t),\ (2/3,-1/3-t),\
                                      (-1/3+t,2/3).
 \end{split}
\]
The counterclockwise middle vertices are
\[
 \begin{split}
 &(-1/3-t,1/6+t/2),\quad(-1/3,-1/3),\\
 &(1/6+t/2,-1/3-t),\quad(2/3,-1/3),\\
 &(1/6+t/2,1/6+t/2),\quad(-1/3,2/3).                 \tag{1}
 \end{split}
\]
These are six of the nine endpoint vertex averages. To verify that
none of the other averages lies outside their hull, take the
cross product of each oriented edge in (1) with the vector to each
of the nine averages. The resulting possible values are exactly
\[
 0,\quad t,\quad (1+3t^2)/4,\quad
 (1+t)(1+3t)/4,\quad (1+t)/2,\quad
 (1-t)(1+3t)/4.
\]
All are nonnegative. The successive edge turns are positive for
0<t<1/3, so this also verifies the ordering and the actual hull
description without a numerical hull calculation.

The endpoint and middle areas are
\[
 w(t)=\frac{1+3t^2}{2},\qquad W(t)=\frac{1+3t}{2}.
\]
Thus total mixed mass is
\[
                 M(t)=\frac32(1+t+2t^2).             \tag{2}
\]

## 2. Exact masses of the unchanged three caps

Retain
\[
 H_0=\{-x-y\ge0\},\qquad H_1=\{x\ge0\},\qquad
 H_2=\{y\ge0\}.                                     \tag{3}
\]
Their margins sum to zero, so they cover the entire ambient space
for every t and every common positive dilation of the source.
The determinant-one map R(x,y)=(-x-y,x) commutes with J and
permutes the vertices of K. It preserves A_t,B_t,D_t and cyclically
permutes the three caps. Consequently all three cap masses agree.

At each endpoint, x>=0 isolates the vertex (2/3,-1/3±t).
The other two vertex x-coordinates are -1/3±t, so its area fraction is
\[
                 f(t)=\frac4{9(1-t^2)}.             \tag{4}
\]
For the middle, the two intersections with x=0 have y-coordinates
±(1+3t)/[3(1+t)]. Together with the three x-positive middle vertices
in (1), they give by shoelace
\[
 |D_t\cap H_1|=\frac{(1+3t)(2+3t)}{9(1+t)},\qquad
 f_0(t)=\frac{4+6t}{9(1+t)}.                         \tag{5}
\]
All cuts are proper and their boundaries have area zero in every
fiber. The common GLOBAL cap mass is therefore
\[
 \begin{split}
 D(t)&=2w(t)f(t)+W(t)f_0(t)\\
 &=\frac{6+7t+12t^2-9t^3}{9(1-t^2)}.                 \tag{6}
 \end{split}
\]
At t_0=1/10, (2) and (6) recover
\[
                  M_0=42/25,\qquad D_0=6811/8910.
\]

## 3. Strict monotonicity of the normalized cap budget

Put R(t)=D(t)/M(t). Direct differentiation gives
\[
 R'(t)=
 \frac{2P(t)}
 {27(1-t^2)^2(1+t+2t^2)^2},                          \tag{7}
\]
where
\[
 P(t)=1+12t-4t^2+44t^3+45t^4+48t^5-18t^6
     =1+4t(3-t)+44t^3+9t^4(5-2t^2)+48t^5.
\]
Every term in the last expression is positive or nonnegative on
0<t<1/3, and the constant term is positive. Hence R'(t)>0 on the
entire chamber. This is an exact sign certificate.

Reducing the rotation separation therefore lowers the common cap
fraction. The raw mass also changes, so one must keep the dilation
cost; decreasing t without normalization is not the claimed escape.

## 4. A smooth strict escape in every neighborhood

Fix any t_0 in (0,1/3), and choose 0<t<t_0. Since R(t)<R(t_0),
\[
 \frac{M_0}{M(t)}<\frac{D_0}{D(t)}.
\]
Choose the common squared continuous dilation
\[
 q(t)=\frac12\left(\frac{M_0}{M(t)}
                         +\frac{D_0}{D(t)}\right),
 \qquad L(t)=\sqrt{q(t)}.                            \tag{8}
\]
Use L(t)A_t,L(t)D_t,L(t)B_t as the actual fibers. Their convex hull
has precisely these fibers, because common dilation commutes with
the Minkowski average. The integer coordinates are unchanged.

The total mass and each of the three cap masses become
\[
 \begin{split}
 M_{\rm new}(t)&=q(t)M(t)
                  =\frac12 M_0+\frac12 D_0/R(t)>M_0,\\
 D_{\rm new}(t)&=q(t)D(t)
                  =\frac12 M_0R(t)+\frac12 D_0<D_0. \tag{9}
 \end{split}
\]
The caps in (3) are unchanged and still cover the entire space.
All actual fiber identities and the active midpoint equality are
preserved exactly.

Moreover L(t_0)=1 and all vertices depend smoothly on t near t_0.
Thus these improvements occur in every neighborhood of the original
source with no cap motion at all. With s=t_0-t as the forward path
parameter, the first derivatives at s=0 are
\[
 \frac{dM_{\rm new}}{ds}
       =\frac{D_0R'(t_0)}{2R(t_0)^2}>0,\qquad
 \frac{dD_{\rm new}}{ds}
       =-\frac{M_0R'(t_0)}2<0.                      \tag{10}
\]
This is an actual strict first-order escape, not just a positive
formal Hessian.

The selected cover remains inclusion-minimal on the source:
the three vertices of the original centered K occur among the
middle vertices for every t. After dilation they still give
strict witnesses for the three respective cap margins.

## 5. A fully rational finite witness

For the stated trap t_0=1/10, one may avoid the square root in (8)
by taking instead
\[
                    t=9/100,\qquad L=1007/1000.
\]
Its squared scale lies strictly between the two bounds in (8).
Every endpoint and middle vertex is then rational. Exact arithmetic
gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 M_{\rm new}&=\frac{16826115057}{10000000000},\\
 M_{\rm new}-M_0&=\frac{26115057}{10000000000}>0,\\
 D_{\rm new}&=\frac{2271685752437}{2975700000000},\\
 D_0-D_{\rm new}
   &=\frac{892421526211}{883782900000000}>0.           \tag{11}
 \end{split}
\]
The standard-library verifier independently clips all three actual
fibers, checks their areas and cyclic cap identities, verifies the
Minkowski hull, and checks every rational inequality in (11).
It also verifies the polynomial identity underlying (7).

The radial obstruction remains correct: A_t and B_t change their
shapes relative to the fixed cap normals, rather than merely being
rescaled independently about zero. Coordinated alignment changes
the actual endpoint support functions and the exact forced middle
body together. No arbitrary free-fiber variation or hypothetical
compatibility slack is used.
